title: BrightPath Planning - AI Tutor Feature Scoping

transcript.speaker: Renata Silva
transcript.text: I want today's planning session focused on scoping the AI tutor feature - I think it could be a real differentiator for next year's renewal cycle.

transcript.speaker: Grace Eze
transcript.text: Agreed. At a high level there are two versions: a simple version that just answers questions about the current lesson's content, and a more ambitious version that adapts practice problems to a student's specific mistakes.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Bennett
transcript.text: The simple version is maybe three weeks - mostly prompt engineering against our existing lesson content plus a chat UI. The adaptive version is a much bigger lift, probably two to three months, because it needs to track mistake patterns over time.

transcript.speaker: Renata Silva
transcript.text: Given the renewal cycle is in four months, let's scope the simple version for this cycle and treat adaptive practice as a follow-up next year.

transcript.speaker: Grace Eze
transcript.text: That's the right call. Fatima, what does the chat UI need design-wise?

transcript.speaker: Fatima Siddiqui
transcript.text: I'll need about a week for a first design pass - I want it to feel like a helpful tutor, not a generic chatbot. I'll mock up two directions and we can pick one.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Bennett
transcript.text: One technical risk to flag - if a student asks something totally off-topic, we need guardrails so the AI doesn't just make something up or go off the rails. I want to scope time for that.

transcript.speaker: Renata Silva
transcript.text: Good catch, that's non-negotiable for something aimed at kids. Build that in as core scope, not an afterthought.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Bennett
transcript.text: Understood, I'll budget an extra week for guardrails and testing on top of the three weeks.

transcript.speaker: Grace Eze
transcript.text: So four weeks total for the simple version, with Fatima's designs ready in week one.

transcript.speaker: Renata Silva
transcript.text: One open question I keep going back and forth on - do we launch this to all students at once, or pilot with a few partner schools first?

transcript.speaker: Grace Eze
transcript.text: I'd lean pilot, but let's decide once we see the first working version rather than now.

transcript.speaker: Renata Silva
transcript.text: Fair, let's revisit that in three weeks.

transcript.speaker: Grace Eze
transcript.text: I'll get design and engineering kicked off this week.

summary_key_points: The AI tutor feature will launch as a simple question-answering version this cycle, not the more ambitious adaptive-practice version
The simple version is scoped at about four weeks including safety guardrails
Guardrails against off-topic or fabricated answers are treated as core scope, not optional
Whether to launch broadly or pilot with partner schools first will be decided later

action_items.task: Deliver a first design pass for the AI tutor chat UI within a week
Build the AI tutor with guardrails against off-topic or fabricated answers
Kick off design and engineering work on the AI tutor this week

decisions: Scope the AI tutor feature to the simple question-answering version for this renewal cycle, not adaptive practice
Treat safety guardrails as core scope for the AI tutor, not an optional add-on
open_questions: Should the AI tutor launch to all students at once, or pilot with a few partner schools first?
